Backscatter point / BRP¶

Summary¶

BRP finds the surface point used in backscatter mode. There, the transmitter, the surface, and the receiver are almost in a straight line (the signal comes nearly straight back, a retroreflection). So the reflection point is simply where the straight line through the transmitter and receiver meets the Earth’s surface on the receiver’s side. BRP solves that point for every time sample, checks the geometry, and – with a link-budget configuration – works out the received power.

It is the backscatter-mode twin of Specular reflection (which handles the forward specular reflection point). The two share the same stored fields, so the rest of the simulator treats them the same way.

Detailed Module Description¶

The retroreflection line¶

Write the line through the transmitter \(T\) and receiver \(R\) as

(57)¶\[\mathbf{P}(t) = T + t\,\hat{u}, \qquad \hat{u} = \frac{R - T}{\lVert R - T \rVert}.\]

Moving along \(\hat{u}\) with \(t > 0\) goes from the transmitter, past the receiver, toward Earth. The BRP is the first surface point on that side.

Where the line meets the ellipsoid¶

Putting \(\mathbf{P}(t)\) into the WGS-84 ellipsoid equation \((x^2 + y^2)/a^2 + z^2/b^2 = 1\) gives a quadratic in \(t\),

(58)¶\[A\,t^2 + 2B\,t + C = 0,\]

with, for \(T = (x_0, y_0, z_0)\) and \(\hat{u} = (u_x, u_y, u_z)\),

(59)¶\[\begin{split}\begin{aligned} A &= b^2(u_x^2 + u_y^2) + a^2 u_z^2,\\ B &= b^2(x_0 u_x + y_0 u_y) + a^2 z_0 u_z,\\ C &= b^2(x_0^2 + y_0^2 - a^2) + a^2 z_0^2. \end{aligned}\end{split}\]

The selected root must satisfy \(t>\lVert R-T\rVert\), so it is beyond the receiver along the Tx-to-Rx ray. Merely choosing a positive root can incorrectly select an intersection between the transmitter and receiver.

Incidence angle and gates¶

The incidence angle is measured from the local ellipsoid normal \(\hat{n}(S) \propto (S_x/a^2, S_y/a^2, S_z/b^2)\),

(60)¶\[\cos\left(\theta_i\right) = \frac{(R - S)\cdot\hat{n}(S)}{\lVert R - S\rVert},\]

and the sample is kept only if \(\theta_i\) is below max_incidence_angle_deg. Two cheaper gates run first: the Tx-Rx central angle must be below max_central_angle_deg, and – when an antenna is given – the look direction must fall inside the antenna’s steering cone (the retroreflector look direction is parallel to \(R - T\), so this can be checked before solving the quadratic).

Module Assumptions and Limitations¶

  • Backscatter (retroreflection) geometry. The BRP assumes Tx, surface, and Rx are collinear. This is the right point for the ocean/ship backscatter mode, not for the forward specular reflection point (use Specular reflection for that).

  • Selected Earth model. earth_model="elliptical" uses the WGS-84 ellipsoid and its geodetic normal. earth_model="spherical" uses the configured mean Earth radius and a radial normal.

  • Coarse central-angle gate. max_central_angle_deg is a quick reject, not the physical horizon.

  • One Tx-Rx pair per object, like Reflection.

Validation and Tests¶

Test group

What it checks

TestEllipsoidIntersection

The BRP lies on the Tx-Rx line and on the ellipsoid; the sub-point case is correct; too-far-apart and Earth-missing geometries are rejected; the selected root is beyond the receiver; identical Tx and Rx is handled; spherical and ellipsoidal modes use their requested surface.

TestAntennaFovPreGate

A nadir BRP passes the field-of-view gate, a far-off-nadir one is rejected, and no antenna skips the gate.

Public interface¶

class object_definitions.BackScattPoint_def.BRP(gps_index, leo_index, *, max_central_angle_deg, max_incidence_angle_deg, earth_model='spherical', gnss_const=None)[source]¶

Bistatic reflection point (BRP) for the backscatter mode, one (Tx GNSS, Rx LEO) pair.

In backscatter mode the transmitter, the surface point, and the receiver are nearly in line (a retroreflection), so the reflection point is where the straight line through Tx and Rx meets the Earth’s surface on the receiver side. This class solves that point at every time sample, applies the geometry gates, and (with a link-budget configuration) evaluates the received power. It is the backscatter-mode counterpart of Reflection.

Parameters:

  • gps_index (Any) – Transmitting (GNSS) satellite identifier.

  • leo_index (Any) – Receiving (LEO) satellite identifier.

  • max_central_angle_deg (float, keyword-only) – Maximum Tx-Rx geocentric central angle [deg]; a coarse geometric gate.

  • max_incidence_angle_deg (float, keyword-only) – Maximum incidence angle at the BRP [deg]; rejects too-grazing geometry.

  • earth_model ({"spherical", "elliptical"}, optional) – Surface model (default “spherical”).

  • gnss_const (str, optional) – GNSS constellation label.

refl_ECI_vec¶

BRP positions in ECI [m], shape (n, 3); NaN where no valid point.

Type:

numpy.ndarray

refl_ECEF_vec¶

BRP positions in ECEF [m].

Type:

numpy.ndarray

refl_LL_vec¶

BRP positions as (latitude, longitude) [deg].

Type:

numpy.ndarray

refl_ang_vec¶

numpy.ndarray

dict

power¶

numpy.ndarray or None

compute_brp_coordinates(GNSS_state, Sat_state, times, tx_eirp_dbw, antenna=None, frequency_hz=None, link_budget_settings=None, q_sat=None, compute_link_budget=True)[source]¶

Solve the BRP at every sample and (optionally) evaluate the link budget.

Fills the reflection attributes in place. Samples failing the central-angle gate, the antenna field-of-view pre-gate, the ellipsoid intersection, or the incidence-angle gate are left as NaN.

Parameters:

  • GNSS_state (Satellite) – Propagated transmitting GNSS satellite (ECI positions / velocities).

  • Sat_state (Satellite) – Propagated receiving LEO satellite (ECI positions / velocities).

  • times (numpy.ndarray) – UTC timestamps aligned with the propagated states.

  • tx_eirp_dbw (float) – Transmit EIRP for this (constellation, band) [dBW].

  • antenna (RxAntenna or None, optional) – Receiver antenna (drives the field-of-view pre-gate; None => isotropic 0 dBi).

  • frequency_hz (float or None, optional) – Carrier frequency [Hz]; defaults to GPS L1.

  • link_budget_settings (dict or BistaticLinkBudgetSettings or None, optional) – Rx-system link-budget settings.

  • q_sat (numpy.ndarray or None, optional) – Attitude quaternion [w, x, y, z] (default identity).

  • compute_link_budget (bool, optional) – If False, skip the link budget (deferred per-event mode); default True.

object_definitions.BackScattPoint_def.calculate_ellipsoid_intersection_t(tx_ecef, rx_ecef, *, max_central_angle_deg, a=6378137.0, b=6356752.314245179)[source]¶

Intersect the line through Tx and Rx with the WGS-84 ellipsoid; return the near-side surface point past Rx.

The line is parameterised as tx_ecef + t * u, with u pointing from Tx toward Rx. The accepted root must satisfy t > |Rx - Tx|, placing the surface point beyond the receiver toward Earth.
